dhp209:1: He who abandons himself to the distractions of this world,
dhp209:2: He who fails to apply himself to his religious duties,
dhp209:3: He who abandons the real purpose of life, he who grasps at what is dear to him,
dhp209:4: Such a man will come to envy him who applies himself to his religious duties.
dhp210:1: Never abide in the company of those who are dear or of those who are not dear;
dhp210:3: It is painful, both to be deprived of the sight of those who are dear, and to be obliged to look upon those who are not dear.
dhp211:1: Therefore hold nothing dear; for the loss of what is dear is an evil.
dhp211:3: Fetters exist not for those to whom naught is either dear or not dear.
dhp212:1: From thought of one that is dear, arises sorrow;
dhp212:2: From thought of one that is dear, arises fear.
dhp212:3: He that is free from thought of dear ones neither sorrows nor fears.
dhp213:1: From affection springs grief; from affection springs fear.
dhp213:3: He that is free from affection neither sorrows nor fears.
dhp214:1: From lust springs grief; from lust springs fear.
dhp214:3: He that is free from lust neither sorrows nor fears.
dhp215:1: From love springs sorrow; from love springs fear.
dhp215:3: He that is free from love neither sorrows nor fears.
dhp216:1: From desire springs sorrow; from desire springs fear.
dhp216:3: He that is free from desire neither sorrows nor fears.
dhp217:1: If a man possess the power to discern between good and evil,
dhp217:2: If he abide steadfast in the Law, if he speak the truth,
dhp217:3: If he perform faithfully his own duties, he will be held dear by the multitude.
dhp218:1: If a man desire the Ineffable, if his heart thrill with desire for the Ineffable,
dhp218:3: If his heart be free from attachment to the Five Lusts, he is called One Bound Up-stream.
dhp219:1: When a man who has long been absent, returns safely from afar,
dhp219:3: Kinsfolk and friends and well-wishers greet him on his return.
dhp220:1: Just so, when a man who has done good deeds goes from this world to the next,
dhp220:3: The good deeds he has performed receive him even as kinsfolk receive a dear friend who has returned home.
